text.headline: US stocks slump as growth worries mount
text.tone: A sharp weekly retreat in equities and industrial metals suggests deepening concerns about the global economic trajectory and trade stability.
lead: US large caps fell 4.6% on Friday, bringing the weekly decline to 9.9% on the [[markets|Financial Markets]] page. This retreat coincided with a rise in the VIX volatility index in the latest data. The EB Shariah US 100 also dropped during the final session of the week.

The pattern across assets is consistent with growing caution regarding global growth. Copper fell 2.7% on Friday, while silver dropped 7.4%. Because more than half of silver demand is industrial, it often trades alongside factory metals. The yen firmed against the dollar, a typical move when investors reduce risk. The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] currently classifies the regime as risk-off.

While trade and geopolitical headlines are consistent with these moves, they remain unconfirmed as primary drivers. Bitcoin rose 3.7% on Friday despite the equity sell-off, suggesting it is moving on its own drivers. On the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]], gold fell, which is contrary to its usual role as a safe haven.

The next few sessions will clarify if this trend persists. Further declines in the 10-year Treasury yield, which fell 3 basis points in the latest data, would strengthen the growth-worry interpretation. A recovery in equities would suggest a short-term adjustment.

briefs.markets: US large caps lost 9.9% this week as the VIX volatility index climbed to 28.44 in the latest data on the [[markets|Financial Markets]] page.
briefs.energy: Brent crude rose 3.1% for the week in the latest data, though US natural gas fell 3.1% on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]].
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin gained 3.7% on Friday, diverging from equities, while the dollar strengthened against the yuan on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] terminal.
briefs.metals: Silver and platinum fell 7.4% and 4.3% respectively on Friday, leading a broad retreat in commodities on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]].
briefs.estate: The [[estate|Estate Index]] shows divergent global trends, with house prices rising in 61 countries while falling 6.3% in China.
briefs.corporate: The [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]] identifies APA Corporation as a top-scoring firm during a week where credit spreads remained relatively calm.
briefs.outlook: The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] notes that semiconductors have fallen 24.8% this quarter, contributing to a broader risk-off environment for global equities.
briefs.islamic: The EB Shariah US 100 fell 10.0% this week, though its year-to-date return of 2.7% remains ahead of the broader market on the [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] page.

watch: Federal Reserve policy developments, as news volume has increased 2.63x normal levels without a corresponding reaction in the latest interest rate or currency markets.
European political shifts and ECB leadership changes, which have seen high news volume but have yet to trigger significant moves in the euro or regional assets.
The 10-year Treasury yield, which sat at 5.04% in the latest data, to see if it continues to fall alongside equities and industrial commodities.
